title: Effect of obesity on arithmetic processing in preteens with high and low math skills. An event-related potentials study
description: This EEG dataset comprises electrophysiological recordings from 62 obese and non-obese preteens performing a delayed-verification arithmetic task. The study investigates the effect of obesity on neural processing of mathematical cognition in children with varying math proficiency levels using 128-channel high-density electroencephalography. Raw event-related potential data were acquired without preprocessing to enable flexible analysis approaches.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a Geodesic Net Amps 300 system with 128-channel Geodesic Hydrocell Sensor Net (Magstim EGI, Eugene OR, USA) running Netstation 4.5.2 software. Stimuli were presented using E-Prime software (Version 2) during a delayed-verification math task at the Arkansas Children Nutrition Center. Participant characteristics including age, gender, body mass index (BMI), and task performance are documented in the Participants.tsv file.
